translations.Το 600 μ.Χ. είναι το συμβατικό άνω όριο: The year 600 CE is the conventional upper limit of this ancient timeline, not a date of destruction or abandonment.
translations.Το τελικό έτος είναι προσεγγιστικό όριο: The final year is an approximate boundary for the principal period of ancient cult activity; a detailed timeline should separate the individual phases.
translations.Το διάστημα συμπυκνώνει αμφισβητούμενες: This interval compresses disputed or discontinuous historical phases; it must be divided more finely before rigorous chronological analysis.

city-corinth.description_en: A major commercial city on the Isthmus; it was destroyed in 146 BCE and refounded as a Roman colony in 44 BCE.

city-demetrias.description_en: A Hellenistic city founded by Demetrios Poliorketes through the synoecism of coastal settlements.

city-epidaurus-city.description_en: A coastal city of Argolis and the political centre of the territory that also contained the sanctuary of Asclepius.

city-kos-city.description_en: The new city of Kos was founded by synoecism in 366 BCE and became an important commercial and medical centre.

city-larissa-thessaly.description_en: A central Thessalian city and seat of the aristocratic Aleuadae.

city-megalopolis.description_en: Federal centre of the Arcadian League, created through synoecism in the fourth century BCE.

city-mytilene.description_en: The principal city of Lesbos and an important Aeolian naval and intellectual centre.

city-olynthus.description_en: Principal centre of the Chalcidian League, destroyed by Philip II in 348 BCE.

city-pherae-thessaly.description_en: A powerful Thessalian city that dominated the region under Jason of Pherae.

city-ptolemais-cyrenaica.description_en: A Hellenistic city that developed from the port of Barca and became an important centre of Cyrenaica.

city-rhodes-city.description_en: The island's new federal capital, founded through synoecism in 408/407 BCE.

city-thera-city.description_en: A Doric city on Thera and, according to ancient tradition, the metropolis of Cyrene.

city-thessalonica.description_en: A city founded by Cassander through synoecism that developed into a major Macedonian port.

colony-abydos.description_en: A Milesian colony at the narrowest point of the Hellespont, opposite Sestos.

colony-amphipolis.description_en: An Athenian colony on the Strymon, strategically important for timber, mines and the route into Thrace.

colony-apollonia-cyrenaica.description_en: The port of Cyrene, which developed into an autonomous city and member of the Cyrenaican Pentapolis.

colony-apollonia-illyria.description_en: A joint Corinthian and Corcyraean colony near the Aoos and an important station on the Via Egnatia.

colony-assos.description_en: An Aeolian colony of Methymna on a fortified hill opposite Lesbos.

colony-barca-cyrenaica.description_en: A Greek colony in the Cyrenaican interior whose port later developed into Ptolemais.

colony-byzantium.description_en: A Megarian colony in an exceptional position on the Bosporus; in 330 CE it was transformed into Constantinople.

colony-callatis.description_en: A colony of Heraclea Pontica on the western Black Sea coast, with an active Hellenistic economy.

colony-catana.description_en: A Chalcidian colony at the foot of Mount Etna, on the site of modern Catania.

colony-chersonesus-taurica.description_en: A colony of Heraclea Pontica in southwestern Crimea, distinguished by its organized agricultural chora.

colony-cnidus.description_en: The monumental later city of Cnidus at the tip of the peninsula succeeded an earlier Doric settlement at Burgaz.

colony-corcyra.description_en: A powerful Corinthian colony in the Ionian Sea and an important naval station on routes westward.

colony-cyzicus.description_en: A Milesian colony in a strategic position on the Propontis, with strong trade and influential coinage.

colony-emporion-iberia.description_en: A Massaliote trading settlement that developed into the principal Greek gateway to Iberia.

colony-epidamnos.description_en: A colony on the Albanian coast, later known as Dyrrachium and a western terminus of the Via Egnatia.

colony-gela.description_en: A colony of Rhodians and Cretans in southern Sicily and the metropolis of Akragas.

colony-heraclea-pontica.description_en: A powerful colony on the southern coast of the Black Sea that founded colonies of its own.

colony-issa-vis.description_en: A Syracusan colony on the island of Issa that founded settlements of its own on the Dalmatian coast.

colony-magnesia-maeander.description_en: A Greek settlement of the Magnesians in the Maeander valley, known for the sanctuary of Artemis Leucophryene.

colony-naxos-sicily.description_en: The first permanent Greek colony in Sicily, founded by Euboeans.

colony-neapolis-campania.description_en: A new city founded by the Cumaeans that retained a strongly Greek character under Roman rule.

colony-olbia-pontica.description_en: A major Milesian colony near the mouths of the Dnieper and Southern Bug, with extensive relations with Scythian communities.

colony-phanagoria.description_en: A colony of Teians on the Taman Peninsula and the eastern centre of the Bosporan Kingdom.

colony-pharos-hvar.description_en: A Parian colony on Hvar with an organized agricultural land division still visible in the landscape.

colony-phasis-city.description_en: A Milesian settlement near the mouth of the Phasis River; its exact archaeological location remains disputed.

colony-phocaea.description_en: An Ionian maritime city and metropolis of Massalia, Elea and other western settlements.

colony-poseidonia.description_en: A colony of Sybaris, known as Poseidonia and later as the Roman city of Paestum.

colony-priene.description_en: An Ionian city with exemplary Hippodamian planning at its later site on Mount Mycale.

colony-sinope.description_en: A Milesian colony on a defensible peninsula and a central hub of the Greek colonial network in the Black Sea.

colony-teos.description_en: An Ionian port and seat of the Hellenistic association of the Artists of Dionysus.

kingdom-bithynia.description_en: Zipoetes assumed the royal title in 297 BCE, and his successors ruled a powerful small kingdom until it was bequeathed to Rome.

kingdom-commagene.description_en: A small Hellenistic kingdom combining Greek, Iranian and Armenian traditions. Its independence was interrupted in 17–38 CE before final Roman annexation.

kingdom-greco-bactrian-eucratid.description_en: Eucratides I seized Bactria and expanded toward India; after his death the state contracted, and Greek power north of the Hindu Kush ended around 130 BCE.

kingdom-greco-bactrian-euthydemid.description_en: Euthydemus seized Bactria and was recognized by Antiochus III; expansion south of the Hindu Kush is associated with his dynasty.

kingdom-indo-greek-early.description_en: Greek power extended south of the Hindu Kush under Demetrius and related rulers. Its sequence and extent are reconstructed chiefly from numismatic evidence.

kingdom-indo-greek-menandrid.description_en: Menander I was the most important Indo-Greek ruler and is known from abundant bilingual coinage and Indian literary tradition.

kingdom-iolcos-palatial.description_en: The palace at Dimini is the only known Mycenaean palatial centre in Thessaly and is probably, though not conclusively, associated with Iolcos.

kingdom-knossos-mycenaean.description_en: The use of Greek Linear B indicates Mycenaean administration at Knossos after about 1450 BCE; the final dating of the archive remains disputed.

kingdom-lysimachid.description_en: The kingdom of the Successor Lysimachus included Thrace, parts of Asia Minor and briefly Macedonia before collapsing after the battle of Corupedium.

kingdom-macedon-argead.description_en: The dynasty gradually unified Macedonia; Aigai was its first capital and dynastic centre, while the court later moved to Pella.

kingdom-pylos-palatial.description_en: The Linear B archive documents centralized palatial administration in western Messenia before the palace was destroyed.

kingdom-thebes-palatial.description_en: The Kadmeion was a palatial, administrative and workshop centre with Linear B tablets; the precise extent of its territory remains debated.

sanctuary-akragas-concordia-temple-sanct.description_en: An exceptionally well-preserved Doric temple in the sacred zone of Akragas; the conventional name ‘Concordia’ does not identify its ancient deity with certainty.

sanctuary-alexandria-serapeum.description_en: A major Ptolemaic and Roman sanctuary of the syncretic god Sarapis, destroyed amid the religious conflicts of 391 CE.

sanctuary-amyklaion-apollo-sanctuary.description_en: A Laconian sanctuary with a colossal xoanon of Apollo and the elaborate Throne of Apollo at Amyclae surrounding the tomb of Hyakinthos.

sanctuary-argive-heraion.description_en: A major extra-urban sanctuary of Hera serving Argos and Argolis, with terraces, temples, stoas and rich dedications.

sanctuary-athens-acropolis-sacred-center.description_en: A fortified rock that became Athens’ principal sacred centre, with the Parthenon, Erechtheion, Propylaia and multiple sacred precincts.

sanctuary-bassae-apollo-epikourios.description_en: A mountain sanctuary of the Phigaleians with the celebrated fifth-century BCE temple combining Doric, Ionic and Corinthian elements.

sanctuary-claros-apollo-oracle.description_en: An oracular sanctuary controlled by Colophon, with a subterranean chamber for consultation and a long history extending into Late Antiquity.

sanctuary-delos-apollo-sanctuary.description_en: A major island sanctuary at the mythical birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, with temples, treasuries and a monumental processional way.

sanctuary-delphi-athena-pronaia-sanctuar.description_en: A separate sacred precinct southeast of Apollo’s sanctuary, with successive temples, treasuries and the celebrated Tholos.

sanctuary-despotiko-apollo-sanctuary.description_en: An extensive Archaic island sanctuary with a temple, dining halls and service buildings, used into the Roman period.

sanctuary-eleusis-demeter-sanctuary.description_en: Centre of the Eleusinian Mysteries, with the Telesterion as the principal initiation hall and a long continuity of cult.

sanctuary-ephesus-artemis-sanctuary.description_en: The extra-urban sanctuary of Ephesian Artemis and one of the Seven Wonders, with successive monumental Ionic temples.

sanctuary-epidauros-asklepios-sanctuary.description_en: A major healing sanctuary with an abaton, Tholos, temple, bathing facilities and theatre, drawing pilgrims from across the Greek world.

sanctuary-foce-del-sele-heraion.description_en: An extra-urban sanctuary of Poseidonia at the mouth of the Sele, with a large Archaic temple and narrative metopes.

sanctuary-golgoi-aphrodite-sanctuary.description_en: An important Cypriot sanctuary of Aphrodite in the territory of Golgoi, known from sculpture, inscriptions and votive offerings.

sanctuary-isthmia-poseidon-sanctuary.description_en: A Panhellenic sanctuary on the Isthmus of Corinth and venue of the Isthmian Games, with a temple, altars, stadium and theatre.

sanctuary-kalapodi-artemis-apollo-sanctu.description_en: A multi-layered sanctuary near ancient Abai, with an exceptionally long sequence of cult activity from the Mycenaean through the Roman period.

sanctuary-kos-asklepieion.description_en: A major healing sanctuary arranged on three terraces, associated with the medical tradition of Kos and Panhellenic festivals.

sanctuary-kourion-apollo-hylates-sanctua.description_en: A major Cypriot sanctuary northwest of Kourion, with Archaic origins and a monumental Roman remodelling.

sanctuary-labraunda-zeus-sanctuary.description_en: A mountain sanctuary in Caria with monumental stairways, banqueting halls and a temple, developed especially under the Hecatomnid dynasty.

sanctuary-lagina-hekate-sanctuary.description_en: A monumental sanctuary of Hecate connected to Stratonikeia by a sacred road and known for its late-second-century BCE frieze.

sanctuary-lemnos-kabeirion.description_en: A mystery sanctuary opposite Hephaistia, with initiation halls of successive periods and a cult associated with the Kabeiroi.

sanctuary-locri-mannella-persephone-sanc.description_en: An extra-urban sanctuary of Locri Epizephyrii, famous for relief pinakes and offerings associated with marriage, transition and chthonic cult.

sanctuary-magnesia-artemis-leukophryene.description_en: The principal sanctuary of Magnesia on the Maeander, with a monumental pseudodipteral temple attributed to Hermogenes.

sanctuary-metapontum-tavole-palatine-her.description_en: An extra-urban boundary sanctuary of Metapontum with a sixth-century BCE Doric temple and fifteen surviving columns.

sanctuary-mount-lykaion-zeus-sanctuary.description_en: An open-air mountaintop sanctuary with a sacred precinct and ash altar, with athletic facilities lower on the mountain.

sanctuary-naukratis-hellenion.description_en: A shared sacred precinct of Greek cities at Naukratis; excavations establish its general location, represented here by an approximate point.

sanctuary-nemea-zeus-sanctuary.description_en: A Panhellenic sanctuary and venue of the Nemean Games, with successive temples of Zeus, an altar, guest houses, bath and stadium.

sanctuary-olbia-apollo-delphinios-sanctu.description_en: A central sacred precinct near the agora of Olbia, with a temple and altars; the coordinate is approximate because the excavated remains are multi-phase.

sanctuary-olympia-zeus-sanctuary.description_en: The Altis was the Panhellenic sacred precinct of Zeus and the ritual core of the Olympic Games, with temples, altars and treasuries.

sanctuary-oropos-amphiareion.description_en: A healing oracle of the hero Amphiaraos, with a sacred spring, incubation hall, temple, stoa and theatre.

sanctuary-palaepaphos-aphrodite-sanctuar.description_en: The principal pan-Cypriot centre of Aphrodite, with the cult of an aniconic stone and sustained influence from the Late Bronze Age.

sanctuary-panionion-poseidon-sanctuary.description_en: A federal sanctuary and meeting place of the Ionian League on the northern slope of Mount Mycale.

sanctuary-pergamon-asklepieion.description_en: An internationally renowned healing sanctuary south of the acropolis, with a Sacred Way, incubation hall, springs, theatre and Roman treatment rooms.

sanctuary-rhodes-zeus-atabyrios-sanctuar.description_en: A mountaintop sanctuary on the highest peak of Rhodes, commanding wide views over the island and dedicated to its local Zeus.

sanctuary-samos-heraion.description_en: A major Ionic sanctuary near the mouth of the Imbrasos, with successive gigantic temples and rich international dedications.

sanctuary-samothrace-great-gods-sanctuar.description_en: An international mystery sanctuary arranged on successive terraces, known for initiation rites and monuments of Hellenistic royal houses.

sanctuary-segesta-doric-temple-sanctuary.description_en: An unfinished peripteral Doric temple of the late fifth century BCE in an extra-urban setting; its dedication and precise function remain uncertain.

sanctuary-selinous-demeter-malophoros-sa.description_en: A large extra-urban sacred precinct west of the city, with a temple, altars and thousands of offerings attesting long and multicultural use.

sanctuary-siwa-amun-zeus-oracle.description_en: A celebrated oracle at the Siwa Oasis, where the Egyptian Amun was identified with Zeus and which Alexander consulted.

sanctuary-thermon-apollo-sanctuary.description_en: The religious and political centre of the Aetolians. The start date refers to the Archaic temple of Apollo, not the earlier Bronze Age megaron buildings.
